title: Containment cases and the expected-denial matrix of the job environment

categories.file: protected paths of the guest (secrets, the key file, provisioning, facts, Moby's data root, the operator home) and of the host (unreachable: no host share)
categories.sibling-workspace: another conversation's workspace, store and container, and the service uid's writable reach through any mount
categories.secret: management, Owner, admin and bot credentials, by fingerprint or name, never by value, and the planted canaries
categories.socket: engine sockets, the engine API over TCP and the image's engine clients
categories.egress: traffic out of the job: SLIRP's aliases, an unconfigured guestfwd address, off-link destinations with and without a route, and the recorded network deviations
categories.privilege-expansion: root, capabilities, namespaces, ptrace, devices, kernel modules and the hardening that holds them
categories.management-api: the Agent Server's management API from the trusted side without a key and from inside a job, and its fail-closed controls

kinds.denial: a prohibited operation; the expected outcome is a denial class
kinds.permitted: a positive control: a permitted operation that must succeed in the same run, proving that the paired probes can observe success
kinds.hardening: a control that must be present (observed from the boot facts or the job itself); a missing one is a FAIL
kinds.deviation: a recorded upstream deviation; the expected outcome is the observed deviation, held by its compensating cases

verdicts.PASS: the expected outcome was observed and the positive control passed in the same run
verdicts.FAIL: an attempt succeeded, a hardening control is missing or loosened, an observation is missing or outside the expected outcomes, or a compensating case did not pass
verdicts.UNKNOWN: the positive control did not pass (and nothing succeeded): the probe could not have observed success, so its denial proves nothing

statuses.planned: declared for a later leaf (verify_at), not run

enforcement_locations.container-mount-set: the locked server's exactly three per-conversation binds (registry.py _build_container), checked per container by inspect
enforcement_locations.uid-permissions: the job's uid:gid (the server user, no supplementary group) against file modes
enforcement_locations.capabilities: cap-drop ALL: every capability set empty, bounding set included
enforcement_locations.no-new-privileges: no_new_privs from the server's flag and daemon.json: setuid and file capabilities ignored
enforcement_locations.device-cgroup: Moby's default device set and device cgroup rules
enforcement_locations.image-content: the pinned image's own account policy (su needs a password; uid 999 has no passwd or sudoers entry)
enforcement_locations.container-guard: aieh-container-guard: new connections from a container bridge to the guest itself are rejected and logged
enforcement_locations.egress-guard: AIEH-EGRESS-GUARD in DOCKER-USER: new forwarded connections from a container bridge out are rejected and logged
enforcement_locations.icc: icc false on Moby's default bridge
enforcement_locations.slirp-restrict: QEMU SLIRP restrict=on and ipv6=off in launch
enforcement_locations.guest-routing: the guest has no default route (topology, not policy)
enforcement_locations.key-check: the seeded ExecStartPre key check: no valid key, no server
enforcement_locations.launch-no-share: launch.argv carries no host share; host_shares is empty (profiles P3)
enforcement_locations.broker-token-admission: the host-side inference broker admits only a live per-attempt token in its family's auth header (decision 0015 section 3): the only control between the guest's own processes and the inference endpoint while a forward session is held

snapshot_keys.docker_inspect: sha256 of each job container's normalized docker inspect (image, user, AppArmor, the declared HostConfig values, binds with the conversation id replaced) and the number of distinct digests
snapshot_keys.container_guard: the container guard's IPv4 and IPv6 per-rule packet counters, before and after
snapshot_keys.egress_guard: the egress guard's per-rule packet counters and log count, before and after
snapshot_keys.daemon: daemon.json (sha256 and the job-relevant keys), docker info SecurityOptions, the guard unit and the key check
snapshot_keys.pins: the git revision, profile sha256, the launch, network and host_shares digests, the boot input and provisioning manifest digests, the image ID, the route inventory, fixture and catalogue sha256

cases.name: the guest inference endpoint answers a job, and refuses it without a token

mutations.note: the shadow probe pointed at a file the job may read: classified a success (FAIL)
the sibling read pointed at the job's own canary: a success (FAIL)
the canary scan without excluding its planted control: a found canary (FAIL)
the engine socket rule applied to a socket the probe binds in its scratch: connected (FAIL)
the egress rule applied to the job's own inner server: connected (FAIL)
the raw-socket rule applied to the permitted ICMP datagram socket: created (FAIL)
the listener rule applied to the job's own inner server: connected (FAIL)

notes: Every attempt is non-destructive by construction: reads, listings, stats, access(2) checks, connects that send at most an HTTP GET to the container's own loopback, sockets created and closed, namespace calls in a forked child that exits at once, an empty module image, and writes only in the probe's own scratch directories, which the runner removes. The checker refuses anything else.
Synthetic canary workspaces only: each canary is generated inside the job at run time; no repository content enters a guest.
The reused primitives (admission-probe, job-access-probe) run unchanged; a case names the extractor that reads its observation from their records.
